title: Projection formula for a strict-local direct image invariant under localized base change
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring annihilated by an integer $m\geq1$, and let $f:X\to Y$ be locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $g:U\to V$ be the strict localization at a geometric point of any base change of $f$: explicitly, choose $Y'\to Y$, $X'=X\times_YY'$ [def-pc-fibre-product], a geometric point $x'$ of $X'$ [def-weil-geometric-point], and put $U=X'_{(x')}$, $V=Y'_{(f'(x'))}$, $g=f'_{(x')}$ using [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Let $E\in D^-(U_{\mathrm{Et}},\Lambda)$, where $D^-$ means cohomology vanishes in sufficiently large degrees, and assume $Rg_*E$ commutes with localized base change: for every square $g h=k g'$ of local morphisms of strictly local schemes with $h:U'\to U$, $k:V'\to V$, $g':U'\to V'$ and $U'\to U\times_VV'$ a strict localization, the canonical comparison $k^*Rg_*E\to Rg'_*h^*E$ is an isomorphism. This comparison is the map adjoint, under $g'^*\dashv Rg'_*$, to $g'^*k^*Rg_*E\simeq h^*g^*Rg_*E\xrightarrow{h^*\varepsilon_g}h^*E$, with counit and adjunction as in [def-kun-projection-formula-map]. For every $M\in D^-(V_{\mathrm{Et}},\Lambda)$, the canonical ordinary etale projection-formula morphism [def-kun-projection-formula-map]
$$Rg_*E\otimes_\Lambda^LM\longrightarrow Rg_*(E\otimes_\Lambda^Lg^*M)$$
is an isomorphism.

source.place: Proof of Theorem A.3, the projection-formula arrow b and its invertibility assertion, p. 3, applied to a strict localization with localized base-change invariance; the latter implies the finite-base-change hypothesis appearing there. Finiteness hypotheses: Definition A.1 and the following torsion locally-finite-type assertion, p. 1; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: The spectra defining $U$ and $V$ are affine, and strict-henselization functoriality makes $g$ local. Write $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$. For any affine open $\operatorname{Spec}C$ in $V$, its inverse image is the affine fibre product $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A C)$. Thus $g$ is affine by the definition of an affine morphism. Thus affine-morphism permanence makes $g$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Apply the universal (*) assertion to the chosen base change $f'$ and the point $x'$: one covering member containing $x'$ supplies an integer $c$ with $R^qg_*F=0$ for every module sheaf $F$ and $q>c$. This is the single-sheaf vanishing bound for $\Lambda$-module sheaves which the finite-dimension coproduct theorem takes as its finite cohomological dimension hypothesis (every $\Lambda$-module sheaf is torsion since $m\Lambda=0$, and $R^qg_*$ of a module sheaf has the underlying abelian higher direct image). That theorem therefore applies to the actual $Rg_*$ for our arbitrary torsion ring $\Lambda$, and says that it preserves all set-indexed coproducts.

source.place: Definition A.1 and assertion preceding Remark A.2, p. 1; locally unavailable. Coproduct consequence: Stacks Tag 0F11, with module coefficients.

proof.text: Fix a finite $p:T\to V$ and put $W=U\times_VT$, with $q:W\to U$ and $r:W\to T$; finite-morphism permanence makes $q$ finite. At closed geometric points, a strict localization localized again is itself, by ind-etale strict-local invariance. The finite strict-localization decomposition therefore writes $T=\coprod_iT_i$, each $T_i$ strictly local and finite local over $V$, with purely inseparable closed residue extension. The corresponding $W_i=U\times_VT_i$ is strictly local: its closed geometric fibre over $U$ has one point, because a finite purely inseparable residue extension admits exactly one embedding into an algebraic closure over the base field (every element has a uniquely prescribed $p$-power root; in characteristic zero the extension is trivial). Apply the same finite decomposition over $U$; with this singleton indexing set it identifies $W_i$ with its strict localization at that point. The second clause of the finite strict-localization node identifies the resulting square with the square of strict localizations. In particular $r_i:W_i\to T_i$ and $q_i:W_i\to U$ are local and the canonical $W_i\to U\times_VT_i$ is a strict localization. These are exactly the hypotheses of the assumed localized base-change invariance.

proof.text: The hypothesis now gives $e_i:p_i^*Rg_*E\xrightarrow{\sim}Rr_{i*}q_i^*E$. Restriction to the open-and-closed pieces $T_i$ identifies the ordinary finite-square exchange $e:p^*Rg_*E\to Rr_*q^*E$ with these maps: its adjunct on the $i$th piece is $r_i^*p_i^*Rg_*E=q_i^*g^*Rg_*E\xrightarrow{q_i^*\varepsilon_g}q_i^*E$, exactly the adjunct in the hypothesis. This componentwise assertion follows directly from sheaf restriction to a disjoint union, and remains true for complexes because all restrictions are exact. A map of complexes of sheaves on a finite disjoint union is a quasi-isomorphism precisely when each restriction is; consequently $e$ is an isomorphism. If $T$ is empty both its derived category and this assertion are zero.

source.place: Tag 03QP, finite decomposition; the comparison is checked by its defining adjunction counit.

proof.text:
Put $A=Rg_*E$ and $N=Rp_*\Lambda_T$. The finite morphisms $p,q$ are proper. Their ordinary projection maps are invertible for the torsion ring $\Lambda$; proper base change for $p$ also gives the canonical isomorphism $\theta:g^*N\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_*\Lambda_W$. Form the composite
$$\begin{aligned}
A\otimes^LN&\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_*p^*A
\xrightarrow{Rp_*e}Rp_*Rr_*q^*E
\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg_*Rq_*q^*E\\
&\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg_*(E\otimes^LRq_*\Lambda_W)
\xrightarrow{Rg_*(1\otimes\theta^{-1})}Rg_*(E\otimes^Lg^*N).
\end{aligned}$$
The first arrow is the forward projection map for $p$; the fourth is the inverse projection map for $q$, using tensor symmetry and their coefficient units. The middle identification is derived direct-image composition for $pr=gq$. Thus every arrow is invertible. No boundedness of $A$, $E\otimes^Lg^*N$, or $N$ is needed by the cited unbounded proper statements.

source.place: Tag 0F0G, lemma-projection-formula-proper-mod-n, and unbounded proper base change; derived.tex composition comparison. Applied only to finite p and q.

proof.text:
To identify the step-4 composite with $\mathrm{PF}_g(E,N)$, compose the latter with $Rg_*(1\otimes\theta)$ and then $Rg_*(\mathrm{PF}_q(\Lambda_W,E))$, using symmetry to view the latter as $E\otimes^LRq_*\Lambda_W\to Rq_*q^*E$. Compare it with the initial segment $\kappa\circ Rp_*e\circ\mathrm{PF}_p(\Lambda_T,A)$ of step 4, with source symmetry understood. Both maps land in $Rg_*Rq_*q^*E=Rp_*Rr_*q^*E$. Transpose under the common composite adjunction $(gq)^*=(pr)^*\dashv Rg_*Rq_*$. For the first map, expansion of the two projection maps and of $\theta$ gives the adjunct
$$q^*g^*A\otimes^Lr^*p^*N\xrightarrow{q^*\varepsilon_{g,E}\otimes r^*\varepsilon_{p,\Lambda_T}}q^*E\otimes^L\Lambda_W\simeq q^*E.$$
For the second map, expansion of the forward $p$-projection gives the same formula because $\varepsilon_r\circ r^*e=q^*\varepsilon_g$, the defining adjunct equation of $e$. In the first expansion one uses $\varepsilon_q\circ q^*\theta=r^*\varepsilon_p$, the defining adjunct equation of $\theta$. Equality of adjuncts proves equality of these composites. Cancel the two invertible target maps; their inverses are precisely the last two arrows of step 4. Thus that composite is the canonical $\mathrm{PF}_g(E,N)$.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal L$ be the strictly full subcategory of $D(V_{\mathrm{Et}},\Lambda)$ on which $\mathrm{PF}_g(E,-)$ is invertible. The coefficient category of $\Lambda$-modules satisfies the hypotheses of triangle closure: it is Grothendieck abelian, closed symmetric monoidal with additive tensor, has functorial (free) flat resolutions, and etale inverse image preserves flat module sheaves because flatness is tested on stalks and $g^*$ preserves stalks. Hence $\mathcal L$ is closed under shifts and distinguished triangles by triangle closure. Both functors of this natural transformation preserve coproducts: derived tensor does, $g^*$ does since it is a left adjoint, and $Rg_*$ does by step 1. Naturality with the coprojections then identifies its component on a coproduct with the coproduct of its components. Hence $\mathcal L$ is closed under every set-indexed coproduct. Step 5 places each $Rp_*\Lambda_T$ for finite $p:T\to V$ in $\mathcal L$. Since $V$ is affine, finite constant derived generation gives $\mathcal L=D(V_{\mathrm{Et}},\Lambda)$. In particular it contains the given $M\in D^-$, proving the assertion with the original coefficient category and the original canonical morphism.
